issue.title: TUI Agents page clips settings when an agent has many model fields (e.g. omp)
issue.body:
### Summary

On the TUI's `1 agents` page, each agent is rendered as a single line containing
every configured field. Agents with many model fields (omp has model, subagents,
smol, slow, plan, vision, advisor, commit, tiny, memory, plus per-role thinking
levels) produce a line far wider than the terminal. The fields past the right
edge are not visible in the agents overview.

The fields are still operable — `Right`/`Tab` cycles `m.col` through all fields
and `Enter` opens the selected field's picker — but because the row never wraps
or scrolls horizontally, the selected field can itself remain off-screen. There
is no way to see the clipped values in the overview.

### Environment

- magpie 0.1.1318 (Linux x64)
- omp 18.12.5

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install omp and configure several model roles, e.g. `model`, `task`, `smol`,
   `slow`, `plan`, `vision`, `advisor`, `commit`, `tiny`, `memory`.
2. Run `magpie` and press `1` to open the agents page.
3. Look at the omp row.

### Actual

All fields are concatenated into one line. With 10 role models the row exceeds
the terminal width; only the first few fields are visible and the rest are cut
off. Long values (full model ids such as
`magpie/opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, or omp fallback lists like `a,b:high`)
widen the row further.

### Expected

Every configured field should remain readable in the overview regardless of
terminal width. Reasonable options:

- wrap a row's fields onto indented continuation lines, aligned under the agent
  name; or
- truncate the row with an ellipsis and show the full set of fields for the
  selected agent (e.g. in the detail/footer area or a scrollable pane).

In either case the selected row's marker and the agent path should stay visible.

### Root cause

`viewList()` in `internal/tui/tui.go` builds the row as

```go
line := pad + marker + name + "  "
for j, f := range a.Fields {
    ...
    line += cell + " "
}
 ```

 and never compares line against m.w (only the optional path suffix checks
 for room). The view is emitted un-truncated, so the row exceeds the viewport.

 Evidence is synthetic: a temporary unit test called viewList() with one
 omp-like agent (10 fields) and m.w = 80, and the generated row measured
 478 cells wide. I did not run the TUI in real terminals at other widths.

 ### Suggested regression test

 Render viewList() at a narrow width (e.g. 80) with an agent that has more
 fields than fit on one line and assert that all labels/values are still present
 in the output (across wrapped lines), or that truncation is explicit and the
 selected field stays visible.

comments.body:
Implemented in the fork: https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/cebfc28361b5b4a29b71d3ddfbdfd039e69c2b96

Expand the selected agent into wrapped field lines when its compact row exceeds the terminal width. The visible field window follows the selected field, keeps the config path visible, and reduces surrounding agent rows so the selection stays on screen. Other wide rows are truncated to fit. No additional scrolling state.

The retained regression fails on the previous implementation and checks all ten model fields with Tab navigation, Unicode values, 30 agents and terminals sized 80x24, 48x12 and 120x40. The full TUI package passed race tests three times. A built Linux binary was also exercised in a real PTY at all three sizes using isolated omp configuration and a fixture executable; all ten model values were reachable through Tab navigation.

Combined verification: https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/348fb7567a74e605e535f07a208fe966b633b45b

Go 1.26.8, umask 027, isolated HOME: native/Linux nogui/Windows vet and builds passed, and `go test -tags nogui ./... -count=1 -timeout=45m` passed on the combined commit above.

The PTY check used a fixture agent, not a live vendor session. Extremely small terminals still abbreviate the agent name and path.


Round 25 check (2026-10-26): this issue was already delivered in the October 23 fix linked above. The later round-25 implementation was duplicate work and is withdrawn as a new delivery. The original branch remains the implementation to use.
